name: Divergent reasoning (custom models) — generation, judge, implement, review, ship
description: divergent-reasoning with the Claude-side models as PARAMS, so presets can dial model strength per task without cloning the blueprint (the 'tough tasks' preset: fable-5 plans + judges, opus-4-8 implements). Grok reasoners stay fixed (grok-build + grok-composer-2.5-fast) for structural diversity. Params: task (the work), cwd (a prepared git worktree — lifecycle is the caller's), orchestrateModel, planModel (Agent A), judgeModel, implementModel (also used by fix/ship — a --resume spawn does NOT inherit the model flag, so pinning it prevents a mid-session downgrade), reviewModel. All five model params are REQUIRED — an unfilled one is passed literally to `claude --model` and fails the node loudly. ||| MODEL-DIVERSITY CORRECTION (2026-08-05): grok CLI 0.2.101 retired grok-build and grok-composer-2.5-fast; `grok models` now lists exactly one model, grok-4.5. Both grok legs therefore run THE SAME WEIGHTS. This workflow's original premise was three distinct families; it is now three independent SAMPLES across TWO families (claude + grok). Independence count 2, not 3 — see papers/agentruntime/invariant-3-independent-verification.md. To restore a third family, repoint reason-grok-fast at `runtime: claude` + `workerProfile: kimi-1` (an ephemeral k3 worker; see review-panel.json). Left as a decision for this workflow's owner, not taken here.

params.prompt:
You are an orchestrator. Your job is to take a task and produce a structured brief that three independent planning agents will work from. Read the codebase in this directory to understand the context.

=== TASK ===
{{params.task}}

Produce a brief with these sections:
PROBLEM: what exactly needs to change and why
SUCCESS CRITERIA: specific, testable conditions that mean the task is done
CONSTRAINTS: what must not break, performance/compatibility requirements, files that must not be touched
SCOPE: what's in scope and what's explicitly out

Be precise. The planning agents will read this brief and the codebase independently — they won't talk to each other.

meta.description: Orchestrator — structures the problem into a crisp brief with success criteria and constraints. Model: {{params.orchestrateModel}}.

params.prompt:
You are an independent planning agent (Agent A). Read the codebase in this directory and produce a concrete implementation plan for the task described below. Name exact files, functions, and the sequence of changes.

=== BRIEF ===
{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

Respond with ONLY the plan. Label it PLAN-A.

meta.description: Agent A — Claude, fresh session, model from planModel. Explores one solution space.

params.prompt:
You are an independent planning agent (Agent B). Read the codebase in this directory and produce a concrete implementation plan for the task described below. Name exact files, functions, and the sequence of changes.

=== BRIEF ===
{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

Respond with ONLY the plan. Label it PLAN-B.

meta.description: Agent B — Grok Build, fresh session. Different weights see a different solution space.

params.prompt:
You are an independent planning agent (Agent C). Read the codebase in this directory and produce a concrete implementation plan for the task described below. Name exact files, functions, and the sequence of changes.

=== BRIEF ===
{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

Respond with ONLY the plan. Label it PLAN-C.

meta.description: Agent C — Grok Composer 2.5 Fast, fresh session. Third independent perspective from a speed-optimized model.

params.prompt:
You are an independent judge. Three planning agents — Claude, Grok Build, and Grok Composer Fast — each produced an implementation plan for the same task, working from the same brief but independently. You have access to the same codebase.

=== BRIEF ===
{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

=== PLAN-A (Claude) ===
{{nodes.reason-claude.result.reply}}

=== PLAN-B (Grok Build) ===
{{nodes.reason-grok.result.reply}}

=== PLAN-C (Grok Composer Fast) ===
{{nodes.reason-grok-fast.result.reply}}

Evaluate each plan against the SUCCESS CRITERIA and CONSTRAINTS from the brief. Check their file/function references against the actual codebase.

Your reply MUST follow this format:
WINNER: PLAN-A or PLAN-B or PLAN-C or HYBRID
REASONING: why, with specific references to the criteria
FINAL PLAN: the complete plan the implementer should execute
BORROWED: what was taken from the other plans (if hybrid)
REJECTED: what was wrong with each losing approach

meta.description: Judge — fresh session, model from judgeModel. Writes the FINAL PLAN the implementer executes; the strongest model should hold this pen.

params.prompt:
You are implementing a plan in THIS directory — an isolated git worktree. The plan was selected by an independent judge from three competing proposals.

=== PLAN ===
{{nodes.judge.result.reply}}

Implement the FINAL PLAN section now. Do NOT commit, push, or open a PR — just make the changes. When done, reply with a summary of what you changed.

meta.description: Implementer — fresh session, model from implementModel. Session resumed by fix and ship nodes.

params.prompt:
You are an independent reviewer. An implementation was made based on a judged plan. You have the original brief with success criteria, and access to the actual files.

=== BRIEF ===
{{nodes.orchestrate.result.reply}}

=== WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED ===
{{nodes.implement.result.reply}}

Read the ACTUAL changed files. Check the implementation against EVERY success criterion and constraint from the brief.

Your reply MUST BEGIN with exactly one token: APPROVE or REJECT.
If REJECT, list each specific problem, the file it's in, and what must change.

meta.description: Reviewer — fresh session, model from reviewModel. Reviews against the orchestrator's success criteria, not the plan.

params.prompt:
A reviewer assessed your implementation:

=== REVIEW ===
{{nodes.review.result.reply}}

If APPROVED, leave the work as-is. Otherwise address EVERY point raised. Do NOT commit or push. Reply with what you changed.

meta.description: Fix — resumes the implementer's session, model pinned to implementModel (a --resume spawn does not inherit the model flag).

params.prompt:
Your work has been reviewed and revised. Ship it:
1. Check what you changed: git status --short
2. Land it — the ONLY approved path:
   bash $(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)/agentruntime/scripts/ship-guard.sh -m 'conventional message' <each changed path>
   It refuses to push main/master, refuses to ship from the shared main checkout, and takes explicit paths only (there is no -A — a shared-index sweep steals other agents' in-flight work). If it REFUSES, STOP and report its message verbatim; do not route around it with raw git.
3. gh pr create --fill --base main

Reply with ONLY the PR URL. If nothing changed, reply: NO-CHANGES.

meta.description: Ship — resumes the implementer's session, model pinned to implementModel. Commits + opens PR.
